vote.q: Day 4. The generator needs 10 liters of gasoline, and the radio says the dead are moving south toward the bay. Where do we go?
opts: Medium run into a warehouse nobody has searched. Harder, and the unknown cuts both ways.
Easy run to a diner nobody has searched. Food is down to two days.
Easy run. The gas station has the 10 liters of gasoline the generator needs.
vote.how: Comment PIER, DINER or GAS (or its emoji) on the Day 4 Reel. One vote per account, your last comment counts.

survivors.name: Sam
survivors.bio: Holed up in the old laundromat on 3rd Street. Hasn’t seen another living person in weeks.

survivors.name: Jaylozy
survivors.bio: Jaylozy joins as a Sharpshooter, ready to take the shot when the moment comes.

survivors.name: Tanny
survivors.bio: Tanny is a professional hiker who knows every trail, making them a natural Scout.
survivors.away_note: scouting the north road toward Millbrook
survivors.away_back: From the overpass he saw them: a column of the dead filling the highway, heading for the bay. Three days out, maybe less.
away_talk: Tanny on the north road. Quiet so far.
Overpass at mile 12. Smoke on the horizon.
Seth, you copy? I can hear them before I see them.
Holy... there are so many. Heading back.

survivors.name: Seth
survivors.bio: Seth manages e-commerce by day and knows his way around IT, so he's ready to keep the radios humming.

survivors.name: Gary Finklestein
survivors.bio: Gary ran a very specialty shop downtown. He knows every back door on Main Street and won't say how.

survivors.name: Adam
survivors.bio: Adam showed up at the gate with a toolbox and grease under his nails. First thing he asked was where the generator is.

survivors.name: Asa
survivors.bio: Asa is a doomsday prepper who swings an axe at the dead and suits up in full armor, because the apocalypse could use a little extra clank.

survivors.name: Gabe
survivors.bio: Gabe is a doctor who plans to keep the whole camp patched up, since the apocalypse is just a bad case of Monday.

survivors.name: Mateen
survivors.bio: Mateen swapped spreadsheets for seed packets and intends to keep the entire camp fed and green.

survivors.name: Jeremy
survivors.bio: Jeremy is a stranded soldier who has been waiting for orders for way too long and is ready to take the shot himself.

survivors.name: Victoria
survivors.bio: Victoria walked in alone from Hollow Creek with a cleaver on her belt. She can make a feast out of a can of beans, and she says the farm out there could feed everyone.

schedule.went: walked south to Hollow Creek Farm to see if Victoria was right
report: {crew} filled their packs from the farmhouse pantry and the rain barrels by the barn.

The crops: two fields of corn and one of wheat are still standing. Cut before the first frost, that's around 60 rations, enough to get the camp through the winter. But something has been moving low in the rows, and {a} didn't want to find out what.

The water pump: the windmill still turns in the wind, but the pump rod is seized and the troughs are dry. {b} thinks a good mechanic could free it in a day. That's 10 rations of water straight away, then 4 clean every night with no fuel.
Cattle tracks lead off through the broken fence into the woods. The greenhouse is full of seed trays. Victoria was right.

schedule.note: Tanny's report changes everything: the horde reaches the laundromat on Day 7. Two days to shore up the fence and find ammo.
The big choice: get ready for what's coming from the north (ammo from the Gun & Pawn, or fortify the fence), or stockpile at Victoria's farm (the windmill pump for water, or the harvest for food).
The front of the Millbrook horde reaches the city: faster ones that turned recently, and dock brutes from the coast.

broadcast.text: ...this is Millbrook... they came through the valley three nights ago... thousands of them... moving south... toward the bay...

highlights.title: Roof garden
